title: Using Seismic Statistical Features and VQ-VAE to Improve Spatiotemporal Seismicity Predictability
abstract: arXiv:2606.10069v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In this paper we build upon a previous study in which we demonstrated, using XGBoost and earthquake catalogue data from Japan and Chile, that a set of 60 seismic statistical features (SSFs) had much greater predictive value than a set of 428 generic time series features from the tsfresh package. We here extend this previous work in two key ways, focusing on data from Japan as a large dataset is necessary in order to allow for the training of a deep learning (autoencoder) model. First, we move from whole-region prediction (considering, for each candidate event, the likelihood of an event M $\geq$ 5.0 anywhere in the region in the next 15 days) to localised predictions in which both the region of feature computation and the region of prediction are restricted to a circle of radius 24 km around the candidate event, and we show that performance remains excellent, similar to our previous whole-region study for the same area. tldr: 该研究将基于60个地震统计特征的预测从全区域扩展到候选事件周围24公里半径的局部化预测，并证明其性能依然出色，同时结合VQ-VAE深度学习模型进一步提升了时空地震活动的可预测性。
en_tdlr: This study extends prior work by shifting from whole-region to localized earthquake prediction within a 24 km radius around candidate events, showing that seismic statistical features retain excellent predictive performance, and leverages VQ-VAE deep learning to further improve spatiotemporal seismicity predictability.
